extracted.intended_audience: pilots, air carriers, air traffic/flight-procedure designers, and FAA/aviation operations personnel
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and required elements for FAA standard instrument approach procedures (ADF, VOR, TerVOR, VOR/DME, ILS, Radar) including units, minima, routing, procedure-turn/missed-approach actions, and operational restrictions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Units and reference conventions
rubrics_metrics.description: Bearings, headings, courses and radials are magnetic. Elevations and altitudes are in feet MSL. Ceilings are in feet above airport elevation. Distances are in nautical miles unless otherwise indicated, except visibilities which are in statute miles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This convention applies to all instrument approach procedure types (ADF, VOR, TerVOR, VOR/DME, ILS, Radar) described on the page and governs how published numbers are to be interpreted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandatory compliance with published procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: If an instrument approach procedure of the above type is conducted at the below named airport, it shall be in accordance with the following instrument approach procedure, unless an approach is conducted in accordance with a different procedure for such airport authorized by the Administrator of the Federal Aviation Agency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Published procedure is mandatory unless specifically authorized otherwise by the Administrator.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initial approach routing and minimum altitudes
rubrics_metrics.description: Initial approaches shall be made over specified routes. Minimum altitudes shall correspond with those established for en route operation in the particular area or as set forth below.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Initial routing and minimum altitudes are part of the published procedure; exceptions only when specifically set forth or authorized.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ceiling and visibility minimums by transition and aircraft category
rubrics_metrics.description: Ceiling and visibility minimums are specified in tabular form for each transition (From—To—Course and distance) and provide minima for aircraft condition categories (2-engine or less; 65 knots or less; more than 65 knots; more than 2-engine, more than 65 knots).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples in the tables include values such as '300-1', '400-1', '500-1', '800-2', 'NA'; these minima vary by transition and aircraft category and must be used to determine landing minima.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure turn specification
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedure turn instructions specify side of course (e.g., E side of crs), outbound and inbound headings (e.g., 134° Outbnd, 314° Inbnd), and altitude to be maintained within a specified distance (e.g., 2600' within 10 miles).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedure-turn entries often include nonstandard notes (e.g., 'Procedure turn nonstandard due to ...'), and specify when a procedure turn is required or when other fixes (e.g., LOM, INT) may substitute.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimum altitude over facility on final approach course
rubrics_metrics.description: Each procedure lists a 'Minimum altitude over facility on final approach crs' (e.g., 2200', 1500', 1300').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This published minimum must be observed on final approach; it is often given alongside course/distance information (facility to airport miles).

rubrics_metrics.name: Missed-approach / failure-to-establish-visual-contact actions
rubrics_metrics.description: If visual contact not established upon descent to authorized landing minimums or if landing not accomplished within X miles of [facility], make specified climbing turn to [altitude] on [bearing] from [facility] within [miles], then return to [facility] and hold on specified radial/course with specified turns and timing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: 'make left-climbing turn to 2600' on 134° bearing from ATW “H ” within 16 miles.'; 'make right-climbing turn to 2500' on 145° bearing from EFW RBn within 10 miles, then return to EFW RBn and hold BE on 325° crs Inbnd in 1-minute pattern with all turns to the right.' These sequences specify exact missed approach climb headings, altitudes, and hold patterns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure turn authorization / prohibition notes
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedures may state when procedure turns are required or not authorized (e.g., 'Final approach from holding pattern at Menasha Int not authorized. Procedure turn required.'; 'Procedure turn authorized for rotary wing aircraft only.').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the published authorization/prohibition: some approaches prohibit procedure turns from certain fixes or reserve procedure turns for specific aircraft types.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alternate minimums for air carriers with weather reporting service
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain alternate lower minimums are authorized for air carriers with weather reporting service at the airport (e.g., 'Alternate minimums of 800-2 authorized for air carriers with weather reporting service at the airport.').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tables and notes designate which minimums apply 'at all times for those air carriers with approved weather reporting service.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Night takeoff/landing runway authorizations
rubrics_metrics.description: Night takeoffs and landings authorization is specified per runway (e.g., 'Night takeoffs and landings authorized on Runways 13-31 only.'; 'Night takeoffs and landings not authorized Runways 18/36.').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operations at night are limited to specified runways when indicated; absence of authorization means night ops are not permitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimums when control zone effective vs not effective
rubrics_metrics.description: Some procedures list separate minimums that apply when the control zone is effective and when it is not (e.g., 'Minimums when control zone effective: ... Minimums when control zone not effective: ...').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply the correct set of minima depending on control zone status; notes often indicate which minima apply 'when control zone effective' and special altimeter/communication requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimum Safe Altitude (MSA) sector altitudes within specified radius
rubrics_metrics.description: MSA within X miles of facility are published by sector (e.g., 'MSA within 25 miles of facility: 000°-090°—1700'; 090°-180°—2100'; ...').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use sector MSAs for emergency or planning purposes within the specified radius (commonly 25 or 26 miles).

rubrics_metrics.name: Facility-on-airport and breakoff-point information
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedures indicate when the navigational facility is located on the airport and provide breakoff points and distances to runway thresholds (e.g., 'Facility on airport. Breakoff point to runway, 170°—0.5 mile.').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this information for final approach planning and for determining when to execute missed approach/landing actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of DME fixes/DME arcs to authorize lower minima or eliminate procedure turns
rubrics_metrics.description: For DME equipped aircraft, specified DME fixes (e.g., 3-mile DME Fix, 8-mile DME Fix) may identify lower minima; when authorized by ATC, DME arcs may be used to position aircraft for straight-in approaches and eliminate the procedure turn.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: 'Following minimums authorized for VOR and DME equipped aircraft and 3-mile DME Fix identified'; 'When authorized by ATC, DME may be used via 8-mile DME Arc ... with the elimination of the procedure turn.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Restrictions and exceptions by aircraft type
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedures include aircraft-type restrictions or exceptions (e.g., 'Procedure authorized for rotary wing aircraft only.'; '400-1% authorized with operative high-intensity runway lights, except for 4-engine turbojets.').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Observe aircraft-type limitations on minima and authorizations; some lower minima or lighting-based reductions exclude certain turbojet categories.

rubrics_metrics.name: ILS-specific minima and glide slope interception criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: ILS procedures specify intercept altitude for glide slope, minimum altitude at glide slope interception (e.g., 'Minimum altitude at glide slope interception Inbnd, 1600'.), altitude of glide slope and distance to approach end of runway at OM and MM, and special minima when glide slope not utilized.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: 'Altitude of glide slope and distance to approach end of runway at OM, 1560'—6.7 miles; at MM, 217'—0.6 mile.'; '*50(h% required when glide slope not utilized.' Follow published ILS-specific notes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Altimeter-setting source requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedures may require altimeter settings from specified Flight Service Stations (FSS) during certain hours (e.g., 'Altimeter setting from Green Bay FSS during hours control zone effective.'; 'Altimeter setting from CMI FSS during hours control zone not effective.').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pilots must obtain altimeter settings from the named FSS when specified by the procedure and during the indicated control-zone status/hours.

rubrics_metrics.name: Terrain and obstacle caution notes
rubrics_metrics.description: Cautions identify terrain or obstacle hazards and their location/height relative to the airport (e.g., 'Caution: 2100' terrain, 2.5 miles S of airport.'; 'Caution: Four (4) towers, highest 3049' located 2.5 miles W of airport.').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Observe published cautions during procedure planning and execution; obstacle/terrain notes may affect minimum altitudes, missed-approach routing, and departure procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pilot IFR flight-plan closure procedure upon reaching contact conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: Pilot will close IFR flight plan with [facility] upon reaching contact conditions and when completion of approach is assured (e.g., 'Pilot will close IFR flight plan with Vero Beach radio upon reaching contact conditions and when completion of approach is assured.').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This procedural instruction is part of the published approach and must be followed when specified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Visibility/minimum reductions tied to runway lighting and limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain reduced visibility minima are authorized only with specific runway lighting operational (e.g., '*400-1 authorized with operative REIL or high-intensity runway lights, except for 4-engine turbojets.'; 'Reduction below 1 mile not authorized.'; 'Reduction below 1/2 mile not authorized for high-intensity runway lights.').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply lighting-based reductions only when the specified lighting is operative, and observe absolute lower-limits stated (e.g., reductions not allowed below specified thresholds or for certain aircraft).
